stewart_read: This is the objection_inversion trigger point: the customer's skepticism (Sunrun couldn't fully offset his bill) is the same financial pain that justifies switching providers. Rep's answer at 05:29 ('we want to offset your entire bill... otherwise it doesn't make sense for you to go solar') is a reasonable value statement but doesn't flip the frame onto the cost of staying with the 6,000 kWh gap he's still paying Sunrun-style shortfall on.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's direct, confident answer may have been sufficient to satisfy the immediate question without needing a rhetorical flip, since the customer moved on to booking right after.
coaching_implication: Show the rep the inversion move: reframe the still-unpaid 6,000 kWh as the actual cost of NOT switching, rather than only promising a better number later.

stewart_read: Rep makes a guarantee claim ('We guarantee savings') at the very end of the call without qualification -- this is a promise a setter shouldn't be making unilaterally, and it becomes a promise the closer now has to honor or walk back.
